mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT keep improving from the recent trough, more daytime movement will spill into nearby shops and malls, lifting RETAIL_REC versus the prior four weeks over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -32.7 to -28.6 while TRANSIT improved from -24.4 to -17.6 between t-3w and t-1w
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC stays below the prior 4-week mean even while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in RESIDENTIAL time signals people are staying home more, reducing discretionary shopping trips and pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is positive and near 9 points in all four weeks
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC rises above its last 4-week average despite RESIDENTIAL remaining elevated for the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM exceeds 5 points above baseline, routine errand trips substitute for discretionary retail visits and RETAIL_REC falls relative to the prior month over the following week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM crosses above +5 and stays there for at least one weekly mean
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from 0.0 to 8.6 from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC does not weaken within one week after GROCERY_PHARM first exceeds +5.

mechanism_narrative: If parks mobility remains depressed while transit also softens, outdoor and mixed-purpose trips stay constrained and retail footfall declines further over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below -30 and TRANSIT remains below -15 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS stayed between -41.4 and -33.1; TRANSIT stayed between -24.4 and -17.6
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC improves while PARKS and TRANSIT both remain below the stated thresholds for two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A continued easing in PARKS mobility indicates warmer leisure conditions and more out-of-home activity, which should support retail visits and raise RETAIL_REC over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -41.4 to -33.1 over the last three weeks
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over four weeks despite PARKS moving upward from its current level.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week drop in TRANSIT of more than 3 points signals access friction or renewed caution, and that shock reduces retail trips within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls by more than 3 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -17.6 to -19.0 at t-0w after improving earlier
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC does not fall within two weeks after a >3 point weekly drop in TRANSIT.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES improves while RESIDENTIAL simultaneously stays high, people return to mixed commute-and-home routines that convert more weekday movement into shopping activity, increasing RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES moved upward overall while RESIDENTIAL stayed positive around 8-10
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC does not outperform the previous 4-week mean while WORKPLACES recovers and RESIDENTIAL remains elevated.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM keeps rising from the current elevated level while RETAIL_REC is still below baseline, the shift reflects substituting essentials for discretionary shopping, so RETAIL_REC will stay weak over the next month.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above +7 for at least two weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM is 7.1 then 8.6 while RETAIL_REC remains near -25 to -24
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC rises above its last 4-week average while GROCERY_PHARM stays above +7 for two weeks.
